instruction: Look up flights departing from Miami to Denver on the 12th of next month and filter to show only flights available for mile redemption.

metadata.explanation: Task variation searching for flights from Miami (MIA) to Denver (DEN) on the 12th of next month, filtered for mile redemption. Uses the same evaluator structure as the original task - extracts flight search details from Delta.com HTML using get_active_tab_html_parse and validates them with check_direct_json_object. The get_rule_relativeTime getter converts '12th next month' to the absolute date format that Delta.com displays.
metadata.verification: The evaluator checks: (1) departure city is MIA, (2) destination city is DEN, (3) date matches the 12th of next month in format 'DoW, Month Day, Year', (4) the 'Miles' tab is active indicating mile redemption filter is applied. All HTML class names match the original Delta.com structure.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: All 4 instruction requirements are verified - (1) departure city MIA, (2) destination city DEN, (3) date on 12th of next month, (4) mile redemption filter active (Miles tab).

Correct semantic extraction: get_active_tab_html_parse (chrome.py:1487) uses appropriate CSS class selectors for Delta.com to extract flight details. The class_multiObject_child config extracts airport codes from 'mach-flight-context-info__wrapper__info--separator' direct text nodes, class_singleObject extracts date from 'mach-flight-context-info__wrapper--date' and active category from 'mach-global-tabs-small__wrapper__tab--active'.

Correct time conversion: get_rule_relativeTime (misc.py:93) successfully handles '12th next month' - it's registered in relativeTime_to_IntDay (misc.py:71) and implemented in the function. The previous fix has been verified and applied. The function converts the relative time to absolute date format '{DoW}, {Month} {Day0D}, {Year}' matching Delta.com's display format.

Correct comparison logic: check_direct_json_object (general.py:382) performs exact key-value matching between extracted result and expected values, which is semantically appropriate for this verification task. The metric will correctly identify if departure/destination airports, date, or category (Miles) don't match expectations.

Data flow is sound: HTML parser extracts {start, end, time, category} → time getter converts relative date to absolute → metric compares all 4 fields → returns 1.0 only if all match, which correctly verifies task completion.
validation.fix_description: Added '12th next month' support to relativeTime_to_IntDay dictionary and implemented the handler in get_rule_relativeTime function following the same pattern as existing next month handlers.
